# Scoring loaves

Scoring cuts the skin of the proofed dough with a razor blade, called a lame, so the loaf expands where you choose instead of bursting at the side. A good score opens into an ear on the crust.

Hold the blade at a shallow 30 degree angle and make one confident slash about a centimetre deep along the length of the loaf, just before it goes into the [[Baking in a dutch oven|dutch oven]].

A single curved slash gives an ear; a cross or a square lets a round boule rise evenly. Cold dough from the fridge scores cleanly.
